questions.question: Which prompt indicates user EXEC on a device named Edge?
questions.explanation: The greater-than sign marks ordinary user EXEC in this IOS prompt.

questions.question: Which command changes Edge> to Edge# after successful authentication?
questions.explanation: enable enters privileged EXEC from user EXEC.

questions.question: At Edge#, which command opens global configuration mode?
questions.explanation: configure terminal enters the global configuration context from privileged EXEC.

questions.question: At Edge(config)#, which command selects an existing routed port for configuration?
questions.explanation: The interface command enters the selected port's configuration context.

questions.question: At Edge(config-if)#, which command returns to Edge(config)#?
questions.explanation: exit steps back one level from interface configuration.

questions.question: Which command leaves Edge(config-if)# and goes directly to Edge#?
questions.explanation: end returns to privileged EXEC from nested configuration modes.

questions.question: Which command displays the active configuration from Edge(config-if)# without leaving that mode?
questions.explanation: do allows an EXEC command to run from a configuration context.

questions.question: You want a console at Edge# to stay connected with ordinary user EXEC privileges. Which command fits?
questions.explanation: disable lowers the privilege level. exit at the EXEC level can close the session.

questions.question: A worksheet says to run hostname Core from interface configuration, then stay in global configuration. Which sequence works?
questions.explanation: exit reaches global configuration, where IOS accepts hostname.

questions.question: Refer to the configuration prompt. Which command changes the current port's description directly from this prompt?
questions.explanation: The config-if prompt provides the context for the description subcommand.
